about.title: About Color Contrast Checker - WCAG AA/AAA Standards
about.description: The Color Contrast Checker evaluates color combinations for accessibility compliance and readability according to WCAG AA/AAA standards. This essential tool ensures your color choices meet web accessibility guidelines for inclusive design, helping designers and developers create accessible interfaces that work for users with visual impairments while ensuring compliance with accessibility standards and legal regulations.

steps.description: Choose your text or foreground color using the color picker or enter HEX/RGB values.

steps.title: Choose Background Color

faq.q: What is a good contrast ratio for accessibility?
faq.a: WCAG guidelines recommend a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text (AA level) and 7:1 for enhanced accessibility (AAA level). Large text (18pt+ or 14pt+ bold) requires 3:1 for AA and 4.5:1 for AAA compliance.

faq.q: Why is color contrast important for web accessibility?
faq.a: Good contrast ensures text is readable for people with visual impairments, color blindness, or when viewing in bright sunlight. It's also legally required in many jurisdictions under accessibility laws like ADA and Section 508.

faq.q: What's the difference between WCAG AA and AAA levels?
faq.a: WCAG AA is the standard level for web accessibility compliance and legal requirements. WCAG AAA is the highest level, providing enhanced accessibility for users with more severe visual impairments, though it's not always practical for all content.

faq.q: How can I improve poor contrast ratios?
faq.a: Make colors darker or lighter to increase the difference between foreground and background. You can darken text colors, lighten background colors, or use our tool's suggestions for achieving better contrast ratios while maintaining your design aesthetic.
